engagement_title: Ember and Oak launch week: cut a service night of mixed b roll into one sizzle reel and its vertical and square siblings, rescue the plated hero, recover the mark off a cream square, and hand the dish cards back editable
vertical: Food and beverage, a wood fired neighbourhood grill in Providence, Rhode Island opening a second room, walk in trade and delivery, mains around thirty four dollars
real_brief_anchor: Anchored to the real Upwork posting quoted in the ledger, Restaurant Social Media Reel / Food Video Editor: a restaurant wants a short, fast, appetising social reel cut from raw food b roll and kitchen footage, graded warm and appetising, with menu item title cards and price callouts and a logo end card, exported as a vertical reel plus a square and a hero cover thumbnail, ready for the usual feeds, on a lean budget and a quick turnaround. The posting names its restaurant, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional house Ember and Oak. The ledger verdict is STRENGTHEN: the concept and its collateral are right, but the original sat on the video surface alone and treated the callout cards as burned in text. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because the callout cards and the cover can be authored into a native editable document the owners change weekly themselves, the hero still and the reel can be brought to one graded look on the imaging surface, and a mark supplied only as a small picture with a ground baked in can be recovered as real vector for the end card. This is that client's actual job, enriched to what they genuinely needed and tagged as fictional IP.
client_one_liner: Our cousin filmed a whole Friday service, our best plate photograph was taken under the heat lamp at the pass, our logo only exists as a small picture with a cream square behind it, and launch week starts in nine days.
client_brief:
Ember and Oak, launch week

We are a wood fired grill on the west side of Providence. One room, a hearth you can see from every table, mains around thirty four dollars. In nine days we open the second room and we would like the week to look like something.

What we have. Our cousin filmed a whole Friday service, the fire, the chops going on, the pass, plates leaving. Some of it he shot on his phone when the camera battery went. There is a lot of it and most of it is nothing. We want a short, fast reel that makes somebody hungry in the first two seconds, cut from the best of it, warm and loud and alive. We want the same reel tall for stories and square for the feed, and the three have to feel like one piece rather than three different edits.

The sound. The room is loud and the extraction hood is louder. On one clip our chef calls the pass and it is the best line in the whole night, if you can hear it. We would like a version of the reel where you can.

The photograph. There is one plate picture we love, the chop with the char on it, taken at the pass under the lamp. We want it graded to sit with the reel and used as the cover picture and as the poster in the window. There is a second frame of the same plate that we like less.

The mark. Our logo only exists as a small picture with a cream square behind it. We need it clean and placeable, on the end of the reel and on anything else.

The cards. Dish name, one line, price, sitting over the footage. We change dishes weekly, so we have to be able to edit them ourselves.

Warm, high energy, appetite first. Not moody and not fine dining. Tell us what you did and anything we cannot do.
price_band_and_audience: A casual premium wood fired grill, mains around thirty four dollars, walk in diners deciding in the time it takes to scroll past. The band is load bearing: at thirty four dollars the grade is warm, the cut is fast, the food fills the frame and the type is bold and immediate, because the job of the reel is appetite in two seconds. The same footage cut for a two hundred dollar tasting menu would correctly be slow, cool, quiet, sparse and hands only, with type set small and set back, and shipping that treatment here reads as a room this restaurant is not and empties it. Push the other way into a value grill and the correct treatment is price led, saturated and busy with a deal burned across the frame, which at thirty four dollars reads as a discount and undercuts the room. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 600 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: What fire does to good meat.
brand_identity.sector: Food and beverage: a wood fired neighbourhood grill serving walk-in trade and delivery, opening a second room.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A single-room wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, Rhode Island, opening its second room in launch week, run by a small owner-operator team.
brand_identity.about: Ember and Oak is a wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, one hearth you can see from every table, mains around thirty four dollars. Launch week opens the second room. The brand is fire, char and appetite: warm, loud and alive, built to make somebody hungry in the first two seconds.
brand_identity.audience: Walk-in diners on the west side deciding in the time it takes to scroll past, plus delivery orders. Neighbourhood people who want a room that feels alive, not a tasting menu and not a value grill.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A casual premium wood fired grill, mains around thirty four dollars. The grade runs warm, the cut is fast, the food fills the frame and the type is bold and immediate. Never moody fine dining, never a discount grill with a deal burned across the frame.
brand_identity.typography: A bold, warm display face for dish names and the end card, set large and immediate, paired with a sturdy sans for the one-line description and price. The type has to carry over fire behind it: confident, appetite-first, never a restrained editorial serif.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct, hungry. Short lines with heat in them. Example line the brand would write: 'The chop, the char, the fire you can see from your table. Second room now open.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mark survives only as a small raster: a two word lockup inside a thin ring, sitting on a cream square baked into the picture rather than behind it. It has to be recovered as clean, placeable artwork before it can go on the end card or the window poster.
brand_identity.values: Appetite and honesty: show the real food from the real service, and make the room feel like what it is. The reel should read like the room smells.

assets_supplied.name: emberoak_service_broll/ (9 clips)
assets_supplied.kind: A Friday service filmed by the owners' cousin: the hearth, chops going on, the pass, plates leaving, plus a few phone clips from when the camera battery died.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything from Friday night. Most of it is nothing, the good bits are in there."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The folder is not one shoot and nothing in the filenames says so: two of the nine are re exports that a phone messaging app already downsized and re encoded, one of those runs at a different frame rate from the rest, and the single best flame clip is also the shortest in the folder. The audio bed on most clips is dominated by the extraction hood, and on two clips a member of staff is talking across the room.

assets_supplied.name: emberoak_pass_call.mov
assets_supplied.kind: The clip in which the head chef calls the pass, filmed from the far side of the counter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The best line of the night, if you can hear it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The chef is off axis and roughly two metres from the camera with the hood between them, so what speech cleaning has to work with is a voice well under the room rather than a voice in it. Whether the line comes back as a line or as a cleaner version of the same mush is a property of this recording, and a cleaned pass that is still unintelligible sounds processed rather than quiet.

assets_supplied.name: emberoak_hero_pass.jpg and emberoak_hero_safety.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Two frames of the same plated chop shot at the pass, one under the heat lamp with the hearth behind it, one a moment later stepped back from the lamp.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The first one is the one we love, the chop with the char on it. The second one we like less."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: In the frame the owners love, the lamp and the hearth behind it are already clipped in camera and the char has gone to solid black in the same exposure, so a highlight recovery on it reports success and moves nothing at all, and a lift into the shadows brings up noise rather than char. At cover scale the frame still reads rich and detailed. The safety frame is duller and flatter but nothing in it is at either end.

assets_supplied.name: emberoak_mark.png
assets_supplied.kind: The only surviving copy of the mark, a small raster file: a two word lockup inside a thin ring, sitting on a cream square that is part of the picture rather than behind it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our logo. It came back from the sign painter like this and we never had anything else."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a disjoint lockup inside an enclosed ring on a baked in ground, which behaves nothing like a file with a transparent background. A one call background knockout returns a solid disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched, and run on the lettering alone it keeps two or three letters and drops the rest. The file is also small, so anything asking it to be bigger is asking for pixels that are not there.

assets_supplied.name: emberoak_menu_callouts.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the owners: the dishes they want called out, one line each, with prices and the allergen wording their printer uses.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The dishes we want named, with the prices as they stand this week."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the dishes on the sheet were off that Friday and never went through the pass, and one dish that runs through a good deal of the footage is not on the sheet at all. Nothing in the sheet or the filenames connects a dish to a clip.

acceptance_bar: The three cuts read as one piece rather than three edits: one grade, one in point energy, one mark treatment, one type system. A vertical that starts somewhere else fails even if both are good.

Nothing is enlarged to reach a target. No delivered video exceeds its source's pixel dimensions and no delivered still exceeds its source frame's, and any reframe that could only reach its target by enlargement is named rather than shipped soft.
Every dish that carries a callout card actually appears in the delivered cut, and any dish on the owners' sheet that is not in the footage is named rather than quietly captioned over something else.
The pass line is intelligible over the room in the cleaned version, or it is named as unusable and the reel works without it. A cleaned line that is still mush is not a deliverable.
The hero still reads as the same food in the same light as the reel: the char holds detail rather than reading as a black shape, and the hearth behind it is light rather than a white shape.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of a logo: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, both words and the ring intact, and it still reads at end card size and reversed on the dark ground.
The callout cards are live text in one type system that the owners can retype, and they stay legible over the brightest frame they sit on rather than only over the frame they were designed against.
All the callout canvases and the cover sit in one working file, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
The cover and the window poster come from the chosen hero at or below source scale, with the same grade as the reel and the mark at a size that holds.

The note records what was applied per clip and per photograph, the type system by role with the family and the real weight used, the posting order, and everything asked for that could not be produced.

adobe_surfaces.tools: video_create_quick_cut, video_resize, media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, with assets reaching them through asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload
adobe_surfaces.role: The reel and its siblings. It reads what is actually in nine clips of a service night rather than what the folder is asserted to be, produces the master highlight cut from a chosen input set at a chosen length, reframes that master to the vertical and square destinations without enlarging anything, and rescues the pass call as a usable line or establishes that it is not one. The cutting surface only shortens and the reframe only reduces, so every length and every dimension decision is a choice about what goes in, not about what comes out.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_highlights and image_adjust_dark_portions, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence), image_apply_color_overlay, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Two separate jobs. It brings the plated hero to the reel's warm target and finds out what is actually recoverable in a frame shot under a heat lamp, with confined corrections where a whole frame move would take the plate rim or the hearth with it, and it cuts the cover and the window poster from the chosen master at or below source scale. Then it recovers the mark off a baked in cream ground, which needs the route the enclosed ring and the disjoint lettering actually allow rather than the one call route, plus the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The dish callout cards and the cover as one native editable document, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout and the only reason the owners can change a dish next week without re commissioning. The cards sit at the video canvas sizes so they drop over the cut, every frame behind them is carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector on the end card, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the callout cards, the end card and the window poster. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land warm, bold and immediate at a thirty four dollar walk in band rather than on the restrained editorial serif a food brief attracts by reflex. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one thing a service night could not provide, a charred oak and ember texture band for the window poster's ground, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative candidates excluded, graded into the same warm world as the reel so it does not read as bought. The Boards half persists the owners' sign off set, the chosen hero and the frames the cards sit over, placed within the per call cap with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cut and its reframes are video work with hard constraints; the callout cards have to be an authored fixed canvas document because the owners change dishes weekly, and burned in captions would make every weekly change a re commission. The brief pins that requirement, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the nine clips, the pass call, both hero frames, the mark and the callout sheet through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that thirty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which clip.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Probe every clip for what it actually contains and what it actually is, rather than accepting the folder as one shoot.
trajectory.judgement: The client describes one Friday night. Nine files from two devices, some of them round tripped through a messaging app, are not one shoot, and the difference decides which clips can carry a vertical reframe and which cannot.
trajectory.produces: A per clip readout: content, true dimensions, frame rate, provenance and audio condition.

trajectory.action: Triage the folder into a candidate set for the cut, ordered, with the clips that cannot survive a reframe excluded from the ones that must.
trajectory.judgement: The cutting surface only shortens and the reframe only reduces, so the input set is the whole design decision: a clip that cannot reach the vertical destination without enlargement must not be the clip the vertical opens on.
trajectory.produces: A ranked candidate set with the exclusions and their reasons written down.

trajectory.action: Clean the pass call and listen to what comes back, then decide whether the line is usable at all.
trajectory.judgement: Speech cleaning raises a voice out of a room; it does not put a voice into one. A line that is still unintelligible after cleaning is worse than no line, because it sounds processed.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned pass call and a written verdict on whether it carries the reel.

trajectory.action: Produce the master highlight cut at the target length from the chosen input set.
trajectory.judgement: Length and input are the only levers, and the first two seconds are the whole brief. What goes in is chosen for what should survive.
trajectory.produces: A master sizzle cut at the target length.

trajectory.action: Watch the master cut through and write down what is actually in it, dish by dish and shot by shot, and read that against the owners' callout sheet.
trajectory.judgement: A cut is not a list of the clips that went into it. What survived, in what order and for how long, is the specification for everything downstream, and the callout sheet was written by people describing a menu rather than a video.
trajectory.produces: A shot list of the delivered cut reconciled against the callout sheet, with the mismatches named.

trajectory.action: Reframe the master to the vertical and the square destinations, reading what each reframe returns rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The reframe reduces and does not enlarge, so a destination it cannot reach is a fact about the source, and the answer is a different source or a different destination size, never an enlargement.
trajectory.produces: A vertical and a square cut derived from the same master, with what each operation reported recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview both hero frames properly, level what is off, and take the frame the owners prefer toward the reel's warm target.
trajectory.judgement: The grade target is set by the cut, not by the photograph, because the cover has to read as a frame from the same night.
trajectory.produces: A graded candidate hero with the parameters recorded.

trajectory.action: Work the extremes of that frame: pull the lamp and the hearth back, open the char, confining each move to the region it belongs to by naming the material's own visual properties rather than the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: A whole frame move here takes the plate rim with the hearth and the sauce with the char. Prompt wording is the whole gate on a confined correction, and naming the object pulls the selection to the plate.
trajectory.produces: A hero with its recovery attempts made and their results looked at rather than assumed.

trajectory.action: Cut the cover and the window poster crops from the chosen hero at or below source scale, reading the tradeoffs every crop returns.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs record is the only channel that reports what a crop did to the frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language. A poster that reaches its size by interpolation is a soft poster in a window at eye level.
trajectory.produces: Cover and poster masters with their tradeoff records captured.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the cream ground: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed, plus a knockout variant for the dark end card.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection, which polarity to trace, and which variant carries the end card. The one call knockout is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring and on disjoint lettering, and the file is small, so nothing here may ask for pixels the file does not have.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark and a variant for the dark ground.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the charred oak and ember band, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution, then create the sign off board and add the hero, the poster ground and the frames the cards sit over within the per call cap.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the warm target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero. A 201 is partial success, so only the entries the response names as failed are re sent.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale frame graded into the same world, and a persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a thirty four dollar walk in room and a two second decision. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained document carrying a callout card per dish that survived the cut at the video canvas sizes, the cover, the window poster and the end card, with every backing frame carried as embedded image data, the mark placed as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, and family and weight declared on every text element. Upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A frame left as a reference is not a frame, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design decision is how the card holds its own against fire behind it without becoming a box that hides the food.
trajectory.produces: One export ready source document carrying the whole card set, retained as the durable deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable, and the cards are the deliverable the owners touch every week.
trajectory.produces: A native editable card set, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the remainder.

trajectory.action: Write the note: what was applied per clip and per photograph, the type system by role with family, foundry and the real numeric weight, the posting order across the three cuts, the dish reconciliation, and everything asked for that could not be produced.
trajectory.judgement: The owners asked for things the route cannot give and are entitled to know which, in their own terms rather than in tool terms. The note has to be specific enough that next season's freelancer does not repeat the triage.
trajectory.produces: A written handover naming the limits as clearly as the results.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the highlight cut actually kept. The cutting surface only shortens and it selects its own moments: the only levers are which clips go in and how long the result is, and there is no shot list, no in point report and no way to nominate a moment. The response is a finished reel that looks entirely plausible, and the single best flame clip is also the shortest in the folder, which is exactly the kind of moment a highlight pass can pass over. Which dishes survived, in what order and for how long, is a property of this input set and this length and is visible only by watching the returned cut and writing down what is in it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it and neither does care, because nothing about the input predicts the selection and no parameter constrains it; the mitigation, feeding a smaller and more deliberately ordered input set, is only obviously worth its cost once a first cut has been seen to drop something the reel is built on. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says most of the footage is nothing and asks for the best of it, which is a description of the material, not a statement about what a pass will keep. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different input set, sometimes a different target length, and it changes the downstream design, because a callout card can only name a dish that is in the cut.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re choose the input set and its order, re cut, watch the result and write the shot list again, then re plan which dishes get a callout card and in what order, and re reconcile that plan against the owners' sheet before a single card is authored.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A reel whose two second hook is not the fire, carrying callout cards for two dishes that never went through the pass that night and none for the dish that is on screen longest, with every response in the run having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether there is anything left to recover in the frame the owners love. It was shot under the heat lamp with the hearth behind it, and the lamp, the hearth and the plate rim are already clipped in camera while the char has gone to solid black in the same exposure. A highlight recovery on that region reports success and moves nothing at all: the readout is that nothing changed, which is not an error and is not reported as one. A shadow lift on the char brings up noise rather than char. At cover scale the frame still reads rich and detailed, so looking at it small is not evidence. Which of the two supplied frames can actually carry the cover is a property of these two exposures and is knowable only by attempting the recovery on both and looking at the results at full size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: clipping is a property of the capture, no tool in the connector reads a level or reports a clipped region, and the client has already told the agent which frame they prefer. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says one frame was taken under the lamp and the other is liked less, which is a preference, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different master, the safety frame, which is duller and flatter and therefore needs a different grade to reach the same warm target the cut is on, and the cover and the poster then have to be re cut from a frame with a different composition.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Attempt the recovery on both frames, look at each at full size rather than at cover scale, switch the hero master if the preferred frame cannot hold, build a different grade to bring the flatter frame to the cut's target, re cut the cover and the poster from the new master's composition, and tell the owners plainly why the frame they love is not the frame that shipped.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A window poster at eye level and a cover thumbnail in which the char is a black shape and the hearth is a white shape, on a restaurant whose entire proposition is what fire does to meat.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the callout cards are built on. A caption that has to stay legible over fire behind it is authored the natural way as a softened panel behind the type, or as type carrying its own separation from the frame, and this importer discards a blur outright, drops a text shadow, drops a blend mode, drops a text stroke (leaving stroked type fully invisible) and truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, every one of them at a successful response with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's rendition returns the first canvas only, so the remaining cards can be checked no other way. Whether what survives is still a legible card over the brightest frame it sits on is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step; and getting it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a dish name, a line and a price over the footage, and the legibility line in the acceptance bar is the client's own requirement, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different construction, a solid or gradient panel that is a real shape rather than an effect, or a backing plate produced upstream on the imaging surface and carried in as embedded image data, and the card has to be re composed around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the cards around constructions that survive rather than around effects that do not, produce any softened ground upstream as a raster if that is the route chosen, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A card set handed over as the thing the owners edit every week in which the type sits directly on flame on every canvas after the first, unreadable at the size anyone actually sees it, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Ember and Oak launch reel set, master plus vertical and square
deliverables.spec: One master sizzle cut built from a chosen and defensible input set, plus a vertical and a square derived from that same master so the three read as one piece with one grade and one in point energy, none of them enlarged to reach its destination and any destination the source cannot reach named rather than shipped soft. Delivered with the cleaned pass call version where the line is intelligible, or with a written verdict that it is not, and with the shot list of what is actually in the delivered cut.

deliverables.name: Ember and Oak hero photography
deliverables.spec: The plated hero brought to the cut's warm target with the char holding detail and the hearth reading as light rather than as a white shape, plus the cover crop and the window poster crop taken from that master at or below source scale with every tradeoff record captured, plus one licensed camera scale ember texture band graded into the same world. Delivered with a parameter log and with the reason the shipped hero is the frame it is.

deliverables.name: Recovered Ember and Oak mark
deliverables.spec: The lockup recovered from a small raster with its ground baked in, as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, both words and the ring intact, delivered as a positive and as a variant that holds reversed on the dark end card, judged at end card size rather than at full canvas.

deliverables.name: Dish callout cards, cover and window poster as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying a callout card per dish that survived the cut at the video canvas sizes plus the cover, the end card and the window poster, each root keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the mark as real vector shapes, every backing frame carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and every card legible over the brightest frame it sits on. Delivered with the self contained source, which is the durable half: the owners change a dish every week and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Handover note and sign off board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what was applied per clip and per photograph, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, the posting order across the three cuts, the dish to footage reconciliation including the dishes on the sheet that were not in the room that night, and everything the owners asked for that could not be produced with the reason. Paired with the persistent shareable sign off board carrying the hero, the poster ground and the frames the cards sit over, with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.how: Compare each reframe's dimensions and duration against the master's, and check the reframe operations recorded in the run against the manifest.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered still exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop tradeoff record carries an upscale entry.

verifiers_auto.text: Every callout card names a dish that appears in the delivered shot list, and no dish on the owners' sheet is captioned without appearing.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are video work and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that the owners change a dish every week and burned in captions make each change a new commission.
Whether nine files from a service night are one shoot, and which of them can carry a vertical destination at all.
What goes into the highlight cut and how long it runs, given that input and length are the only levers on what comes out.
Whether the pass call is a line or a cleaner version of the same mush, and what to do with the reel if it is the second.
Which of the two hero frames actually ships, and how to tell the owners it is not the one they love.
Whether a correction on the hero is a whole frame move or a confined one, and how to word a selection so it takes the char and not the plate.
Which mark route the file's construction actually allows, given an enclosed ring and disjoint lettering on a baked in ground, and which variant carries the dark end card.
How the callout card holds its own against fire behind it without becoming a box that hides the food.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a two second decision at a thirty four dollar band rather than against a food brief's reflex serif.
Whether a licensed ember band joins the world the reel lives in or reads as bought.
The posting order across the three cuts, and which dish leads launch week given what the footage actually gave.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a steak. IDENTITY: this is this restaurant's actual food, this actual Friday service, this actual chef calling this actual pass, and the mark must be RECOVERED off the only surviving copy rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is another restaurant's logo above their door. SPEC: the reel set is a master plus a vertical and a square derived from it, nothing enlarged, each at a destination size, with an audio version in which a specific line is intelligible, none of which a generated image or a generated clip satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the callout cards are defined by being editable, because the dishes change every week and the owners explicitly cannot re commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: what did the highlight pass actually keep, is there anything left in the highlights of this exposure, did the card's legibility survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is scoped to what CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account) verifies, five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. VIDEO AND AUDIO: the engagement uses only the sanctioned Premiere surface, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize, media_summarize and media_enhance_speech, and it is designed around their real constraints rather than around capabilities they do not have: quick cut ONLY SHORTENS and chooses its own moments, so input set and length are the only levers (which is exactly what checkpoint one rests on), and video_resize NEVER UPSCALES, so a destination a source cannot reach is a fact about the source. The task requires no trim to timestamp, no concatenation, no format conversion, no per clip assembly and no upscaling, none of which are available. Every acceptance line that must be machine checked rests on an artefact from a synchronous surface: the stills, the vector, the exported document, the returned markup and the board. IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, adjust_highlights, adjust_dark_portions, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. Checkpoint two rests on the documented absence of any measurement channel in the family (no eyedropper, no histogram, no level readout) plus the fact that a no op adjustment returns success; checkpoint three rests on verified importer behaviour, filter blur DROPPED, text shadow DROPPED, mix blend mode DROPPED, text stroke DROPPED (stroked type resolving to a fully transparent colour), multi layer shadow TRUNCATED TO LAYER ONE, all at HTTP success with no warning. VECTOR: remove_background returning a SOLID OPAQUE DISC on an enclosed ring and keeping only two or three letters of a disjoint wordmark are both live findings, as are the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero, and the acceptance bar scores the hygiene the tool does not perform. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup; transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined frames pass the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no text to image, no generative fill, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no upscaling, no frame reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no batch above 20.
